subject: freediver underwater
title: These People Evolved a Bigger Organ So They Could Hunt Underwater

scenes.text: One group of humans evolved a body part for diving.
The Bajau of Southeast Asia free-dive up to 230 feet with a wooden mask and a spear.
They stay down as long as 13 minutes and spend up to 60 percent of their working day underwater.
In 2018, scientists scanned them. Their spleens were about 50 percent bigger than their neighbors'.
The spleen works like a scuba tank. Hold your breath and it releases extra oxygen into your blood.
Even Bajau who never dive have it. It isn't training. It's in their DNA.

description:
One group of humans has evolved a body part for diving.
The Bajau, the sea nomads of Southeast Asia, free-dive to as much as 70 meters (230 feet) with only weights and a wooden mask, can stay underwater up to 13 minutes and spend up to 60 percent of their working day diving. A 2018 study in the journal Cell used ultrasound to show their spleens are about 50 percent larger than those of the Saluan, a neighboring people who do not dive, and traced the difference to a gene called PDE10A. Bajau who never dive have the larger spleen too. The spleen releases extra oxygen into the blood during a breath-hold, and it is also enlarged in some seals.
How long can you hold your breath? Comment below.
first_comment: The only animals that spend a similar share of their day diving are sea otters. What other human superpower should we look at next?
